text:
Leo Carlsson has 27 points in 21 games, and 18 of them have come on the power play. That's the headline and the caveat at once. Anaheim has built its man advantage around the 21-year-old, and he has answered, but his five-on-five work is closer to break-even: the Ducks hold 49.3% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on, a touch better than the team does without him.

He's a passer first. His six goals come from just 36 shots and 5 expected goals, and his 16.7% shooting sits at the top of our range for him, so the goal total is running a little warm. The assists are a different story. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him among the top passers in the league last season, 94th percentile in primary shot assists, and carrying the puck in on 73% of his entries. Over his last ten he has 14 points against 11.9 expected. What we'd watch is whether the even-strength scoring catches up to the power play, because power-play production swings with whistles, and the playmaking travels.
